A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same InPhyRe study. Their main text, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support comparison. Internal numerical inconsistencies in v2 limit some interpretations but do not prevent identifying changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original zero-shot and few-shot evaluations of 13 LMMs, alongside exemplar-retrieval, quantization and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark experiments and adds proprietary-model evaluations, prompting and fine-tuning experiments, robustness tests and model diagnostics.

M1.justification: The proposed PyBullet/Blender construction pipeline, physical scenario rules, multiple-choice benchmark framework and CLIP-based exemplar retriever are retained. The added prompting, fine-tuning and probing studies evaluate existing techniques rather than introduce a new proposed method component.

E1.justification: The original collision scenarios remain, but v2 adds InPhyRecom with background objects and varying cameras and lighting, modified CC queries requiring visual attribute extraction, and tests exposing the collision outcome through additional frames. Appendix F also evaluates scenario and object-attribute classification from hidden states.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated proprietary comparators: GPT 4.1 Mini, GPT 4.1 Nano, Gemini 2.5 Flash, Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite and Gemini 2 Flash (Table 7). The original open-model cohort remains, and Gemma3-4B gains a row in the corresponding video-only comparison in Figure 5.

E3.justification: Section 3 replaces v1's reserved ten-sample exemplar pool with per-query sampling from the remaining dataset. New protocols include two-demonstration proprietary and full-video evaluations, law-explicit CoT with a 300-token allowance, a fine-tuning epoch/learning-rate grid, and perturbation tests using 100 samples per scenario.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands the analyses with mismatched-video and visually necessary query controls, CoT and fine-tuning interventions, scene-complexity and full-frame tests, prompt perturbations, attention visualization and hidden-state probes. The original exemplar-count, retrieval, quantization and qualitative AMC analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v1 provides no comparable repeated-run or uncertainty reporting. v2 newly states that Section 4 evaluations used three random seeds and reports means, standard deviations and coefficients of variation across ten perturbed dataset versions (Appendix E.10). This does not establish how many runs underlay v1.

E6.justification: Many main results change: Gemma3-4B's regular-LMC three-shot accuracy is 52.46% in v1 Table 1 and 70.70% in v2 Table 2, alongside the revised exemplar protocol. Numerous new experimental results are added. However, v2 retains old Appendix B values: Figure 4 gives Gemma3-4B's LMC difference as +10.63 points, while Table 4 still gives +33.92.

T1.justification: The conceptual distinctions between reasoning types and the mathematical content of the construction pipeline remain unchanged. Neither version presents formal theorems or proofs; v2's standard descriptive statistics and empirical probes do not constitute a theoretical addition.

C1.justification: The benchmark novelty claim and principal findings remain. v2 qualifies the abstract's visual-neglect claim from 'largely ignores' to 'may ignore,' refines Finding 3 around necessary visual reasoning, and adds an introductory claim about CoT and fine-tuning failing on conditional physical reasoning.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations of SB mass ambiguity, conditional-reasoning failures, attention allocation and hidden-state information. Appendices E.5 and F explain why law-explicit prompting and fine-tuning do not cleanly measure induction, and acknowledge that probes cannot establish the failure mechanism or distinguish visual from textual information sources.

D1.justification: v2 adds project-page and dataset-access links, specifies 100-token allowances for verbose outputs and 300 tokens for CoT, and documents full supervised fine-tuning with an epoch/learning-rate grid. It also supplies procedural details for scene perturbations and diagnostic analyses. Existing rendering, model-identifier and hardware disclosures remain.

R1.justification: Section 2 and Appendix C substantially expand the distinction from intuitive, counterfactual and general physical reasoning. New comparisons include IntPhys 2, PhysBench, ContPhy and developmental studies, supported by Tables 1 and 6. Several exemplar-retrieval and RLHF references are removed.

P1.justification: The introduction and related-work narrative are substantially rewritten and reorganized, including moving earlier historical discussion into Appendix C. Section 4.5 becomes a three-experiment narrative, citations switch to author-year format, and an appendix contents page is added. The lengthy original qualitative transcripts remain substantively unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 changes typography, author presentation and page layout throughout. It adds two benchmark-comparison tables, three experimental tables, and displays for the new controls, robustness tests, attention analysis and probes. Existing scenario illustrations and several analysis figures are retained and renumbered rather than newly introduced.

improvement.justification: The new controls in Section 4.5 substantially strengthen v1's language-bias evidence, which relied mainly on removing exemplar QA pairs. Robustness tests and explicit qualifications of prompting, fine-tuning and probing also address important gaps in the original evidence and interpretation. These gains outweigh the reporting defects, especially old Appendix B tables remaining inconsistent with revised main figures, although those discrepancies reduce confidence in exact numerical results.
